x: Article 112 requires the Annual Financial Statement (the Budget) to be laid before both Houses. Article 110 defines a Money Bill, 114 covers Appropriation Bills, and 116 votes on account.
t: Match each Article to its budget role.

x: Option B is incorrect: gender budgeting entered the Union Budget in 2005–06, not 2006–07. The Annual Financial Statement is the main Budget document.
t: Recall the gender budgeting year.

x: Both are true: revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets, and capital receipts do one or the other. A fact about capital receipts does not explain revenue receipts, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a contrast explains the first item.

x: Tax revenue and interest receipts are revenue receipts, while borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts. Because List-II repeats, the key is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Ask whether the item creates a liability or reduces assets.

x: I, II and III are correct: the capital budget has capital receipts and payments, including land, buildings, machinery and loans to States. IV is false because dividends and profits are revenue receipts.
t: Ask whether the item creates a liability or reduces assets.

x: All four are correct: loan recoveries are capital receipts on the capital account, and revenue spending is on the revenue account and creates no liability.
t: Sort each item into revenue or capital account.

x: Market borrowings, Treasury Bills and foreign loans are all capital receipts, and buying shares is a capital payment. The answer is a-i, b-i, c-i, d-iii.
t: Allow codes to repeat.

x: Capital-account items may create a liability or reduce assets. Not doing either is the mark of revenue items.
t: Discriminate capital from revenue items.

x: Corporation tax is tax revenue. Interest, dividends and fees are non-tax revenue.
t: Discriminate tax from non-tax revenue.

x: Option C is incorrect: disinvestment reduces the government's assets, while borrowing creates a liability. Both are capital receipts.
t: Discriminate a liability from an asset reduction.

x: Both are true: borrowings are capital receipts because a capital receipt either creates a liability or reduces assets, and a loan creates a liability. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the definition explains the class.

x: A is true and B is false: salaries and allowances are revenue spending, but disinvestment is a capital receipt that reduces assets.
t: Discriminate tax from non-tax revenue.

x: Corporation tax is tax revenue, interest receipts non-tax revenue, market borrowings a capital receipt, and pensions revenue spending. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Sort each item into its budget head.

x: All four are correct: revenue receipts are tax and non-tax revenue, and income tax, customs and Union excise are all tax revenue.
t: Discriminate tax from non-tax revenue.

x: All four are capital receipts: a loan recovery returns an earlier loan, World Bank loans and market borrowings create a liability, and disinvestment reduces assets. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each receipt to its kind.

x: Capital spending buys, creates, upgrades or extends the life of assets, building long-term productive capacity. The 'only' options describe revenue spending.
t: Discriminate capital from revenue spending.

x: Option B is incorrect: revenue spending does not create assets. Building or buying assets is capital spending.
t: Discriminate capital from revenue spending.

x: Both are true: capital spending builds long-term capacity because it buys, creates, upgrades or extends the life of assets. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the nature explains the effect.

x: Capital spending creates assets, revenue spending does not, non-plan spending covers subsidies, interest and defence, and long-term investment builds capacity. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each type of spending to its feature.

x: All four are non-plan spending: maintaining infrastructure, salaries, pensions and statutory transfers.
t: Recall what non-plan spending includes.

x: Computers are a capital item because they are assets. Pensions, subsidies and interest are recurring non-plan or revenue spending.
t: Discriminate assets from recurring costs.

x: Option D is incorrect: building infrastructure is capital spending. Only its upkeep counts as non-plan or revenue spending.
t: Discriminate building from upkeep.

x: The capital-output ratio is the capital needed to produce one unit of output. Option D reverses the ratio.
t: Watch for an inverted ratio.

x: Option B is incorrect: interest receipts are revenue receipts. Borrowings and loan recoveries are capital receipts.
t: Ask whether the item creates a liability or reduces assets.

x: A is true and R is false: a lower COR raises growth potential because less capital is needed per unit of output, not more.
t: Remember: low COR means high capital productivity.

x: Both are true: a capital receipt creates a liability or reduces assets, and non-tax revenue is a revenue receipt.
t: Discriminate capital from revenue receipts.

x: All four are revenue receipts: tax revenue, interest, dividends and profits, and fees.
t: Ask whether the item creates a liability or reduces assets.

x: A revenue receipt neither creates a liability nor reduces assets, while disinvestment, foreign loans and Treasury Bills are capital receipts. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate capital from revenue receipts.

x: Both are true: a higher COR may slow growth because more capital is needed for each unit of output. R explains A.
t: Remember: high COR means low capital productivity.

x: The FRBM Act was passed in 2003 and came into force on 5 July 2004. The FRBM Review Committee was formed in May 2016 and reported in January 2017.
t: Discriminate the year passed from the start date.

x: Option C is incorrect: the FRBM framework aims to increase transparency in fiscal operations, not reduce it, along with cutting deficits and moving toward a balanced budget.
t: Watch for a reversed objective.

x: Both are true: the FRBM Act aims at fiscal discipline, and it does so by cutting the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit and public debt. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the targets explain the aim.

x: The revenue deficit is revenue spending minus revenue receipts, the fiscal deficit total spending minus non-debt receipts, the primary deficit the fiscal deficit minus interest, and debt management a fiscal-discipline aim. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall each deficit formula.

x: All three are correct: the FRBM Review Committee was set up in May 2016 under N.K. Singh and reported in January 2017.
t: Recall the N.K. Singh Committee.

x: FRBM stands for the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003. The N.K. Singh body is the FRBM Review Committee.
t: Discriminate the Act from the committee.

x: Both are true: better macroeconomic management and moving toward a balanced budget are both FRBM aims. One aim does not explain another, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two aims explain each other.

x: All three are correct: the N.K. Singh Committee proposed capping general government debt at 60% of GDP, with 40% for the Centre and 20% for the States.
t: Recall the 60–40–20 split.
